description: FIND-201's fix (REQ-106's in-process try/catch around `payViaFacilitator`, appending `status:'disbursement_uncertain'` on exception, then reconciling at the start of the next issuance attempt) is NOT a complete guarantee -- it only re-locates the SAME class of hazard one level deeper, into TWO new code paths that are themselves unwrapped and unspecified. (1) The follow-up append itself (`appendChild` for the `disbursement_uncertain` row) is a plain, synchronous `fs.appendFileSync` call (confirmed this session, `~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/ledger.js` lines 20-24 -- no internal try/catch), which CAN itself throw (ENOSPC, EACCES, transient disk failure). If it throws immediately after `payViaFacilitator`'s own catch block already swallowed the settle-side exception, `fn()` propagates THIS SECOND exception uncaught; `withGigLock`'s own `finally` (lock.mjs lines 203-208, confirmed this session) still releases the per-lender lock NORMALLY (via `fs.unlink`), so the NEXT caller takes the fast-acquire path, not the stale-reclaim path. The ledger is left with a 'provisioning' row for this `n` that has NO terminal follow-up at all (neither 'disbursement_uncertain' nor 'disbursement_failed' nor 'active') and a lock that is NOT stale -- a THIRD terminal state the spec's own state machine never anticipates. `nextLoanSequenceForLender`'s own rule ('SHALL NEVER recompute or reuse n for a NEW attempt while a provisioning row for that n exists with no terminal follow-up') has no reconciliation trigger for this exact case: reconciliation is wired ONLY to (a) a stale-lock reclaim finding a 'provisioning' row, or (b) the highest n's row being exactly 'disbursement_uncertain'. A 'provisioning' row with a cleanly-released, non-stale lock triggers neither path, permanently blocking this lender from issuing any further loan with no documented recovery. (2) Symmetrically, `reconcileProvisionalDisbursement` itself performs a real on-chain lookup (`eth_getLogs`/receipt check per an RPC) when invoked 'at the START of the NEXT loan-issuance attempt for this SAME lender... BEFORE computing/using n+1' (lines 782-791) -- this is exactly the same class of effectful, potentially-throwing I/O that caused the ORIGINAL disbursement_uncertain case. The spec's own text describes only the lookup's two SUCCESS outcomes ('finds a matching, finalized Transfer' vs 'finds none') and never addresses what happens if the lookup call ITSELF throws (RPC timeout/network error) when invoked from this NEXT attempt's own `fn()`. Neither REQ-106's EARS text, its Edge Cases, nor its Acceptance Criteria (lines 858-898) contains any SHALL, Edge Case, or Acceptance Criterion covering 'the reconciliation attempt itself throws.' This means FIND-201's own binding claim -- 'so that regardless of whether that call... resolves {ok:true}... resolves {ok:false}... OR THROWS an exception mid-call, a follow-up row is ALWAYS appended by fn() before fn() itself returns or (re-)throws' -- is FALSE for the reconciliation code path it introduces to close the ORIGINAL gap, and is only conditionally true (contingent on a local disk write never failing) for the immediate disbursement_uncertain append itself. This is exactly the scenario the review manifest specifically directs verification of ('an exception thrown from WITHIN the catch block's own reconciliation attempt') and it is confirmed unaddressed.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL THEREFORE wrap step 2 above (the payViaFacilitator call) in its OWN try/catch, INSIDE fn() itself ... so that regardless of whether that call (a) resolves {ok:true} ..., (b) resolves {ok:false} ..., OR (c) THROWS an exception mid-call, a follow-up row is ALWAYS appended by fn() BEFORE fn() itself returns or (re-)throws ... whenever nextLoanSequenceForLender finds the last-appended row for this lender's highest n is 'disbursement_uncertain', THE SYSTEM SHALL ... perform the SAME real on-chain lookup ... BEFORE computing/using n+1.

crossCheck.note: appendChild(file, row) is a plain fs.appendFileSync call with no internal try/catch -- it can genuinely throw (ENOSPC/EACCES/transient I/O failure). Cross-referenced against /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/economy/gig/lib/lock.mjs lines 187-209 (withGigLock's try/finally releases the lock NORMALLY via fs.unlink on ANY exception thrown out of fn(), regardless of which step inside fn() threw) -- confirming that if the disbursement_uncertain append itself throws, the lock is still released cleanly (non-stale), so the next caller takes the fast-acquire path and never triggers reconcileProvisionalDisbursement for this specific 'provisioning, no follow-up, non-stale-lock' state, which REQ-106's own spec text never names or handles.
